lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: estimation and reasonableness

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: In 55,240, compare the value of the 5 in the ten-thousands place with the 5 in the thousands place.

steps: The first 5 represents 50,000 and the second 5 represents 5,000.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Round each number to the nearest hundred to estimate 7177 + 656.
Round 750 to the nearest hundred and 45 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.
A student says 44 × 69 = 3036. Round each number to the nearest ten. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 2810.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 2800.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 3036 and the rounded estimate is 2800.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 3046 and the rounded estimate is 2800.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A student evaluates 8 × [6 + (14 - 4)] + 2: “They multiply 8 by 6 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 60.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The first error is in the final addition or subtraction; the value should be 131.
The student multiplied before evaluating (14 - 4); the innermost difference is 10, giving 130.
The work is correct; 60 is the value.
The grouping symbols do not affect the order; 60 is the value.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 3876654, the value of the 6 in the thousands place is 100 times as much as the value of the 6 in the hundreds place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: Both digits have value 6; repeated digits always have the same value.
The values are 6000 and 600; 6000 is 10 times as much as 600, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
The places are adjacent, so 6000 is 100 times as much as 600.
The values are 6000 and 600; 6000 is 1/10 as much as 600.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Which expression means: “Subtract 7 from 17, multiply the difference by 4, then add 75.”
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Which phrase describes 47 + [8 × (24 - 9)] without evaluating it?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
